_meta.indication: POTIGA is indicated as adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients aged 18 years and older.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Three multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies (referred to as Studies 1, 2, and 3 in the label); the pivotal trials in the reviewer's naming were studies 3065 A1-205, VRX-RET-E22-301, and VRX-RET-E22-302.
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; patients randomized to total daily maintenance dosages of 600, 900, or 1,200 mg/day administered in 3 equally divided doses, with titration from 300 mg/day.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with partial-onset seizures with or without secondary generalization, not adequately controlled with 1 to 3 concomitant AEDs; mean duration of epilepsy 22 years; median baseline seizure frequency 8 to 12 seizures per month.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was the percent change in seizure frequency from baseline in the double-blind treatment phase (criterion for statistical significance P<0.05).
pivotal_trials.result: A statistically significant reduction in median percent 28-day seizure frequency versus placebo was observed with POTIGA at 600 mg/day (Study 1), 900 mg/day (Studies 1 and 3), and 1,200 mg/day (Studies 2 and 3).

nct_ctgov.title: Retigabine (Adjunctive Therapy) Efficacy and Safety Study for Partial Onset Refractory Seizures in Epilepsy

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (vs placebo) were dose-related CNS/psychiatric effects: dizziness (23% overall; 32% at 1,200 mg/day vs 9% placebo), somnolence (22% vs 12% placebo), fatigue (15% overall), confusional state (16% at 1,200 mg/day vs 3% placebo), and tremor (8% overall); urinary retention was reported in approximately 2% (29 of 1,365) of patients and is a labeled warning.
target_moa: Ezogabine is a potassium channel opener; in vitro it enhances transmembrane potassium currents mediated by the KCNQ (Kv7.2 to 7.5) family of ion channels, thereby stabilizing the resting membrane potential and reducing brain excitability.

rems.type: A REMS was required, consisting of a communication plan (Dear Health Care Practitioner letters describing the risk of urinary retention) and a timetable for submission of assessments.

advisory_committee.vote: The drug's potential to cause urinary symptoms, including urinary retention, was discussed at a Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems (PCNS) Advisory Committee meeting held on 8/11/10.

summary.text: Standard NDA 505(b) review. The original NDA (received 10/30/09) received a Complete Response on 11/30/10 for a CMC/nonclinical mutagenic-impurity deficiency; the sponsor submitted a Class 1 complete-response resubmission on 4/15/11, and the application was approved with a required REMS (communication plan) and multiple postmarketing requirements including pediatric and urinary-retention studies.

citations.quote: The Agency issued a Complete Response to the sponsor on 11/30/10; the primary reason for the CR action was stated as follows, taken verbatim from the CR letter:
The sponsor responded to the CR letter with a submission dated 4/15/11.
Your proposed REMS, submitted on June 9, 2011, and appended to this letter, is approved. The REMS consists of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

requirement.text: 1781-3: A prospective cohort study to better define the risk of urinary retention in patients with epilepsy treated with ezogabine, analyzing approximately 2,000 to 4,000 ezogabine-exposed patients.

citations.quote: 1781-3 A prospective cohort study to better define the risk of urinary retention in patients with epilepsy treated with ezogabine and how the risk may vary with demographics (e.g. age), comorbidities that influence voiding (e.g., benign prostatic hyperplasia [BPH], multiple sclerosis) and concomitant medications that may influence voiding. The study will be performed utilizing a research database to compare patients started in two cohorts, those started on ezogabine with those started on other anticonvulsants, for the incidence of urinary retention. The study will analyze approximately 2,000 to 4,000 ezogabine-exposed patients.
